solution: A genus is a group of closely related species that share more characters with each other than with species of other genera; lion, leopard and tiger, for example, are species of the genus Panthera. An individual plant or animal is a single organism, and a population is a group of individuals of one species. A group of closely related families is an order, not a genus. So option C.

NCERT's table of organisms with their taxonomic categories places mango (Mangifera indica) in genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae and division Angiospermae. So family is Anacardiaceae (A-III), genus is Mangifera (B-V), class is Dicotyledonae (C-II), phylum is Angiospermae (D-IV) and order is Sapindales (E-I). So option D.

Ascending order runs from the lowest category to the highest: species (g), genus (a), family (e), order (c), class (b), phylum (d) and kingdom (f). Only option A follows this sequence; the other options mix up the ranks. So option A.

In binomial nomenclature the first word of a biological name is the genus and starts with a capital letter, and the second word is the specific epithet, which starts with a small letter. Statement D swaps the two, so it is not true. Biological names are generally in Latin (A), the two words are printed in italics or underlined separately when handwritten (B), and the specific epithet starts with a small letter (C), so these are true rules. So option D.

Interphase comes first, in the order \(G_1\) phase (the cell grows but does not replicate its DNA), S phase (DNA replication) and \(G_2\) phase (proteins are made in preparation for mitosis). M phase, the actual division, follows interphase. So the sequence is \(G_1\), S, \(G_2\), M, option C.

Statement I is correct: by diakinesis, the last stage of prophase I, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. Statement II is false: it is meiosis II that resembles a normal mitosis, whereas meiosis I pairs the homologous chromosomes and separates them, halving the chromosome number. So option C.

Statement I is incorrect: cells in the quiescent stage (\(G_0\)) remain metabolically active; they only stop proliferating unless called on to do so. Statement II is correct: in animal cells, during S phase DNA replication begins in the nucleus and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. So option D.
why: never said why Statement I is false

solution: M phase is the phase of actual cell division, and mitosis is also called equational division (A-IV). During \(G_2\) phase DNA synthesis stops, but the cell keeps growing and synthesises proteins in preparation for mitosis (B-I). Cells that do not divide further leave \(G_1\) for an inactive stage called the quiescent stage, \(G_0\) (C-II). \(G_1\) phase is the interval between mitosis and the initiation of DNA replication (D-III). So option C.

Matthias Schleiden, a botanist, and Theodore Schwann, a zoologist, together formulated the cell theory (1838 to 1839). Robert Brown discovered the nucleus, Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of the membrane, and Antonie von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. So option A.

The mitochondrion has two membranes that divide its lumen into two aqueous compartments. The inner membrane, folded into cristae, encloses the inner compartment, which is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. Cytosol is the fluid of the cell outside the organelles, and mucus and aqueous humour are not parts of a mitochondrion. So option A.

Cristae are the infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (A-II). Cisternae are the flat, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus (B-IV). Thylakoids are the flat membranous sacs in the stroma of the chloroplast (C-I). Phospholipids, arranged in a bilayer, are the main lipids of the cell membrane (D-III). So option B.

The endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles form the endomembrane system, because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it, since their functions are not coordinated with these organelles. Option A is the only choice without one of these. So option A.

The smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes on its surface and is the major site of lipid synthesis; in animal cells it also makes lipid-like steroidal hormones. Ribosomes on the surface and active protein synthesis are features of the rough endoplasmic reticulum, and carbohydrate synthesis is not the role NCERT gives the smooth ER. So option B.

Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes made of a 50S and a 30S subunit (a), many bacteria carry small circular plasmids outside the genomic DNA (b), and their plasma membrane forms infoldings called mesosomes (c). Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles, so they lack peroxisomes (d). So (a), (b) and (c) only, option D.

Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls, which give parts of the plant yellow, orange or red colours. Chloroplasts mainly hold chlorophyll, while aleuroplasts (which store proteins) and amyloplasts (which store starch) are colourless leucoplasts. So option B.
Starch is the store of energy in plant tissues (A-II). Antibodies fight infectious agents (B-I). Concanavalin A is a lectin (C-IV). GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells (D-III). So option B.

Statement I is correct: mitochondria and chloroplasts are both double membrane-bound organelles. Statement II is incorrect: NCERT describes the inner membrane of the chloroplast as the relatively less permeable one, and says no such thing of the inner mitochondrial membrane, so the statement attaches this property to the wrong organelle. So option C.
why: reasoning not NCERT (ion transport, mitochondria more permeable)

solution: Phyllotaxy is the pattern in which leaves are arranged on the stem or branch. It is usually of three types: alternate (china rose, mustard, sunflower), opposite (Calotropis, guava) and whorled (Alstonia). The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is the inflorescence, and the arrangement of sepals or petals in a bud is aestivation. So option A.

In Solanaceae the flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic (a), the calyx has five united sepals (b), and the five stamens are epipetalous (c). The ovary is superior, bicarpellary and syncarpous, not inferior, so (d) is false. So (a), (b) and (c) only, option A.

(a) is false: the woody, straight and pointed thorns of Citrus and Bougainvillea are modified axillary buds of the stem, not leaflets. (b) is true: the tendrils of cucumber and pumpkin develop from axillary buds. (c) is true: Opuntia has a flattened, fleshy green stem that does the work of leaves. (d) is true: Rhizophora, growing in swampy areas, has roots that grow vertically upwards (pneumatophores) to get oxygen for respiration. (e) is true: the creeping stems of grasses and strawberry spread and form new plants. So (b), (c), (d) and (e), option C.

Both statements are correct. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, the male and female gametophytes of gymnosperms have no independent free-living existence: they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophyte. The ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds that develop after fertilisation are not covered (naked seeds). So option A.

Pteridophytes are divided into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). So Sphenopsida is a class of pteridophytes, option D.

Carrageen is a hydrocolloid obtained commercially from red algae (Rhodophyceae), just as algin is obtained from brown algae. Agar, another red algal product, comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria; NCERT gives the red algal cell wall as cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. Green and blue-green algae are not sources of carrageen. So option C.
why: cell-wall detail not NCERT (agar, carrageen, funori in the wall)

solution: C is the correct pair: the cells of the medullary rays next to the intrafascicular cambium become meristematic and form the interfascicular cambium, which completes the cambial ring. A is wrong: the large, empty, colourless cells in the epidermis of grass leaves are bulliform cells, not subsidiary cells. B is wrong: in dicot leaves the vascular bundles are surrounded by thick-walled bundle sheath cells, not conjunctive tissue. D is wrong: parenchyma cut off by the phellogen that ruptures the epidermis forms lens-shaped openings called lenticels, not spongy parenchyma. So option C.
why: named D's structure complementary cells; NCERT: lenticels

solution: The dark, durable central wood of old trees is heartwood. It is dark brown because organic compounds such as tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils are deposited in the central or innermost layers of the stem (b); these are secondary metabolites, laid down in the dead, highly lignified xylem elements (a). They make the wood hard and resistant to microorganisms and insects. (c) describes cork, with suberin in the outer layers; (d) wrongly places the deposits in the peripheral layers; and (e) describes sapwood, the outer wood that still conducts water. So (a) and (b) only, option A.
why: no reason given for (a); (c), (d), (e) not addressed

solution: Endarch and exarch describe where the protoxylem lies relative to the metaxylem. In stems the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith), which is endarch; in roots it lies towards the periphery, which is exarch. Statement I is incorrect because endarch is the condition of stems only, not a feature of primary xylem throughout the plant body. Statement II is correct because exarch primary xylem is the feature of roots. So option D.
why: no reason given for Statement I being false

solution: In each photosystem all the pigments form a light-harvesting antenna except one molecule of chlorophyll a, which forms the reaction centre. In PS I this chlorophyll a has its absorption peak at 700 nm and is called P700 (in PS II it is P680). Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are accessory pigments that pass the absorbed energy on. So option B.

(a) is wrong: photorespiration occurs in C3 plants; it is C4 plants in which it does not occur. (b) is wrong: in photorespiration \(O_2\) is used and \(CO_2\) is released. (c) is right: RuBisCO binds \(O_2\), and RuBP gives one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one of phosphoglycolate. (d) is right: photorespiration makes no sugar and no ATP or NADPH; rather it releases \(CO_2\) and uses up ATP. So (c) and (d) only, option B.

When RuBisCO binds \(O_2\) instead of \(CO_2\), RuBP gives one molecule of phosphoglycerate (3 carbons) and one molecule of phosphoglycolate (2 carbons). So X is 2-phosphoglycolate. Phosphoenolpyruvate, oxaloacetate and malate belong to the C4 pathway, not to this reaction. So option B.

Priestley (1770) showed that plants restore the air that a burning candle or a breathing animal spoils, which established the role of air. Ingenhousz then showed that sunlight is needed and that only the green parts of plants release oxygen. Julius von Sachs (1854) showed that the green parts make glucose, usually stored as starch. Later Engelmann found that the action spectrum of photosynthesis roughly resembles the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b. So the order is role of air, release of oxygen, production of glucose, absorption spectra: option B.

Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one molecule of \(CO_2\) and uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. A glucose molecule has six carbons, so six turns are needed: \(6 \times 3 = 18\) ATP and \(6 \times 2 = 12\) NADPH. So option A.
why: dropped the 2 in 2 NADPH per CO2

solution: RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase) catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP, the first step of the Calvin cycle, in which \(CO_2\) is fixed (D). Its name records that it can also act as an oxygenase, but it has a much greater affinity for \(CO_2\) than for \(O_2\), so B is false. It is not active only in the dark: the Calvin cycle runs in the light, using the ATP and NADPH of the light reaction, so A is false. Photolysis of water is the work of the water-splitting complex of PS II, not of RuBisCO, so C is false. So option D.
why: non sequitur on affinity; A and C not addressed

solution: Statement I is true: in C3 plants some \(O_2\) binds to RuBisCO, so \(CO_2\) fixation is decreased. Statement II is false: in C4 plants the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO, so they show no photorespiration at all, and in the bundle sheath cells the breakdown of the C4 acid raises the \(CO_2\) concentration, so RuBisCO works as a carboxylase. Photorespiration does not occur in C4 plants. So option C.

A is true: respiration is the breaking of the C-C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within cells. B is false: the first stage, glycolysis, takes place in the cytoplasm; only the Krebs cycle and the electron transport system are in the mitochondria. C is accepted as true: fermentation is the incomplete breakdown of glucose under anaerobic conditions, and plant tissues such as germinating seeds can ferment when oxygen is short. D is true: the fate of pyruvate depends on the cellular needs and the organism, fermentation in many prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes and aerobic respiration in others. E is true: oxygen is the final hydrogen acceptor in the electron transport system and is reduced to water. So A, C, D and E only, option A.

In the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid a molecule of GTP is made by substrate-level phosphorylation; no hydrogen is removed, so the substrate is not oxidised. The other three steps are oxidations: isocitrate to \(\alpha\)-ketoglutaric acid and malic acid to oxaloacetic acid each reduce \(NAD^+\) to NADH, and succinic acid to malic acid (through fumaric acid) reduces FAD to \(FADH_2\). So option C.

Gibberellins promote bolting, the internode elongation just before flowering, in beet, cabbage and many plants with a rosette habit. Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor, indole butyric acid is an auxin known for initiating roots on stem cuttings, and ethephon releases ethylene. So option B.

2,4-D, a synthetic auxin, is widely used as a herbicide to kill dicotyledonous weeds; it does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants, so gardeners use it to prepare weed-free lawns. Kinetin is a cytokinin, abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor and gibberellin is a growth promoter; none of them is used as a weedkiller. So option A.

A is true: all gibberellins are acidic. C is true: zeatin, a natural cytokinin, was isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk. D is true: ethylene induces flowering in mango. B is false: it is abscisic acid, not auxin, that acts as an antagonist to gibberellins. E is false: auxins, not abscisic acid, induce parthenocarpy, for example in tomatoes. So A, C and D, option A.
why: explained only why B and E are false

solution: Gardeners use 2,4-D, an auxin, to kill the broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds in a lawn. It does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants, and lawn grasses are monocots, so the grass is not damaged. Promoting apical dominance (A), causing abscission (B) or helping cell division (D) would not explain why the grass alone survives. So option C.

In non-albuminous (ex-albuminous) seeds the endosperm is completely used up by the developing embryo before the seed matures, as in pea and groundnut. Wheat, maize and barley keep part of the endosperm in the mature seed, so their seeds are albuminous. So option D.
A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, and each lobe has two theca, so the anther is dithecous. A bilobed anther therefore has four microsporangia, located at its corners. So option A.

The two synergids at the micropylar end of the embryo sac bear special cellular thickenings at their micropylar tip, called the filiform apparatus, which guide the pollen tube into the synergid. The antipodals lie at the chalazal end, and the central cell with its polar nuclei takes part in triple fusion, not in guiding the pollen tube. So option B.

The primary endosperm nucleus is formed by triple fusion of a male gamete with the two polar nuclei, each haploid, so the endosperm is triploid (3n). If the diploid number is \(2n = 36\), then \(n = 18\) and the endosperm has \(3n = 54\) chromosomes. So option C.

In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary, as in pea (A-IV). In axile placentation the ovules are attached to a central placenta in a multilocular ovary, as in tomato (B-II). In parietal placentation the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary, as in Argemone (C-I). In free central placentation the ovules are borne on a central axis without septa, as in primrose (D-III). So option D.

A is true: wind- and water-pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar, because they rely on wind and water and do not need to attract animal pollinators. R is also true: the landing of pollen on a stigma is a matter of chance in these plants, so they produce enormous amounts of pollen compared with the ovules available. But the large pollen output makes up for that loss of pollen; it is not why the flowers lack colour and nectar, so R does not explain A. So option B.
why: never said why R does not explain A

solution: A is true: the cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus. R is false: NCERT says the tapetum nourishes the developing pollen grains, and it does not link the extra nuclei to more efficient nourishment of the microspore mother cells. So A is true but R is false, option C.
why: argued that R explains A, against its own key C

solution: Statement I is incorrect: Down's syndrome is caused by an additional copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy of chromosome 21), not by the absence of an X chromosome. Statement II is incorrect: Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes (45 with XO), not by an extra copy of a chromosome. The two statements have the causes swapped, so both are incorrect: option B.

A person with blood group O has the genotype \(ii\), so each parent must pass on an \(i\) allele. In A, B and C both parents carry \(i\) (\(I^A i\) or \(I^B i\)), so an \(ii\) child is possible. In D the father is \(I^A I^B\) and has no \(i\) allele to give, so an O child is not possible. So option D.

When Mendel crossed tall and dwarf pea plants, all the \(F_1\) plants were tall and none was dwarf. This is because stem height is a pair of contrasting traits in which tall is dominant and dwarf is recessive, so only the dominant trait is expressed in the \(F_1\) (law of dominance). So both A and R are correct and R explains A, option A.

Only females are drawn as carriers, and the affected F0 mother with an unaffected father has carrier daughters, which fits an X-linked recessive disorder. In the F2 mating that gives the F3, the mother is a carrier (\(X^cX\)) and the father is affected (\(X^cY\)). Their children are \(X^cX^c\) (affected daughter), \(X^cX\) (carrier daughter), \(X^cY\) (affected son) and \(XY\) (normal son), each with probability \(\frac{1}{4}\). Only \(X^cX\) has no disease and carries the mutation, so the probability is \(\frac{1}{4}\), option A.
why: invented an F1 pedigree member and called the mating consanguineous

solution: Recombination frequency is a measure of the distance between genes, with 1 per cent equal to 1 map unit (centimorgan). Since a-b (20) equals a-c (5) plus c-b (15), gene c lies between a and b. Since c-d (24) equals c-b (15) plus b-d (9), and a-d (29) equals a-b (20) plus b-d (9), gene d lies beyond b. So the order is a, c, b, d, option D.
why: wrong method (decreasing order of recombination frequency)

solution: Kingdom Monera is the only kingdom of prokaryotes; it includes bacteria, cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) and mycoplasma, which have no membrane-bound nucleus. Fungi have a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, so they are eukaryotes. So option D.

The sexual cycle of fungi has three steps: fusion of the protoplasms of two gametes is plasmogamy (A-II), fusion of two nuclei is karyogamy (B-III), and meiosis in the zygote gives haploid spores (C-I). So option A.

Prions are infectious agents made of abnormally folded protein, similar in size to viruses. They cause bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly called mad cow disease, in cattle and its analogue, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), in humans. Viroids are free RNA that cause potato spindle tuber disease, and Aspergillus and Mycoplasma do not cause BSE. So option A.

Bacteria are grouped by shape: spherical bacteria are cocci (A-II), rod-shaped bacteria are bacilli (B-IV), comma-shaped bacteria are vibrio (C-I) and spiral bacteria are spirilla (D-III). So option D.
why: page ref only (and the wrong page)

solution: Lichens are symbiotic, mutually useful associations between algae and fungi: the algal partner (phycobiont) makes food, and the fungal partner (mycobiont) gives shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water. Mycorrhiza is an association of fungi with the roots of higher plants, sponges are animals, and chrysophytes are a group of protists. So option A.

NCERT gives the Amazonian rain forest more than 1,25,000 species of invertebrates, more than 40,000 of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds and 427 of mammals. In descending order this is invertebrates (d), plants (a), fishes (c), birds (b) and mammals (e). So option B.

NCERT records that the Abingdon tortoise in the Galapagos Islands became extinct within a decade after goats were introduced on the island, apparently because of the greater browsing efficiency of the goats. So A is correct and R is correct, and the goats' better browsing, which let them outcompete the tortoise for food, explains the extinction. So option A.

No population can grow exponentially for long, because the resources it needs are finite and become limiting sooner or later. The logistic model allows for this: growth slows as the population nears the carrying capacity (K), giving a sigmoid curve. So the logistic model is considered more realistic, and the finiteness of resources is the reason. Both A and R are correct and R explains A, option A.

In competition both interacting species are harmed (A-III). In predation one species, the predator, benefits and the other, the prey, is harmed (B-I). In mutualism both species benefit (C-II). In commensalism one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited (D-IV). So option D.

Statement I is incorrect: a fig is a plant structure, and the fig wasp larvae that develop inside it do not make it an animal product, so calling it a non-vegetarian fruit is wrong. Statement II describes a real mutualism, but NCERT says the female wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for egg-laying sites, and uses the developing seeds within the fruit to nourish its larvae. It is the inflorescence that gets pollinated, not the fruit, so Statement II is incorrect as worded. Both statements are incorrect, option B.
why: never said why Statement I is wrong

solution: Flamingoes and resident fishes in shallow South American lakes compete for their common food, the zooplankton, which is interspecific competition (A-IV). Chthamalus expands its range on the rocky coast when the competitively superior barnacle Balanus is absent, which is competitive release (C-II). Five closely related warbler species coexist on the same tree by feeding in different parts of it, which is resource partitioning (D-III). That leaves interference competition for the Abingdon tortoise, which became extinct within a decade after goats with greater browsing efficiency were introduced (B-I). Option B is the only choice with this match.
why: no competitive release; non-NCERT label for the tortoise

solution: In the exponential growth equation \(N_t = N_0 e^{rt}\), e is the base of natural logarithms (2.71828). \(N_t\) is the population density after time t, \(N_0\) is the population density at time zero, and r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase. So option C.
why: called r biotic potential; NCERT: intrinsic rate of natural increase

solution: Lactobacillus converts milk to curd, Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast) is used to ferment dough for bread, and Propionibacterium sharmanii makes the large holes in Swiss cheese, so B, D and E are used for household products. Aspergillus niger is used for the commercial production of citric acid and Trichoderma polysporum for cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive agent; both are industrial uses. So A and C only, option B.
why: named S. cerevisiae for toddy (NCERT names no microbe there)

solution: The distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm, that is \(0.34 \times 10^{-9}\) m. Number of base pairs \(= \dfrac{1.1}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 3.2 \times 10^{9}\), about \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\) bp. This matches NCERT, where haploid human DNA has \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\) bp and is about 1.1 m long. So option A.

E. coli divides every 20 minutes, so in 60 minutes there are three generations and the 10 cells become \(10 \times 2^3 = 80\) cells. Replication is semiconservative, so the 20 heavy (\(^{15}N\)) strands of the 10 starting DNA molecules are never broken up: after the first division they sit in 20 hybrid (\(^{15}N\) and \(^{14}N\)) cells, and at each later division every hybrid DNA gives one hybrid and one wholly \(^{14}N\) DNA. So after 60 minutes 20 cells are still hybrid and the other 60 of the 80 cells have DNA totally free of \(^{15}N\). Option C.

In eukaryotes transcription and the processing of its product both take place in the nucleus. The primary transcript (hnRNA) is processed by splicing, the removal of introns and joining of exons (B); capping, the addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end (C); and tailing, the addition of adenylate residues at the 3' end (D). Only the fully processed mRNA is transported to the cytoplasm, so A is not an event at all, and base pairing of two complementary RNAs (E) is not a processing step. So B, C and D only, option B.
why: said transcription occurs in the cytoplasm

solution: Eukaryotes have three RNA polymerases in the nucleus. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S), RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs, and RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). DNA polymerase makes DNA, not RNA. So option B.

The repressor of the lac operon is synthesised all the time, constitutively, from the i gene, so A is correct. B is wrong: lactose, the inducer, binds the repressor and inactivates it, so the repressor cannot bind the operator. C is wrong: i is a separate regulatory gene with its own promoter; only the structural genes z, y and a share the operon's promoter. D is wrong: the inducer is lactose, not galactose. So option A.

Histones are a set of positively charged, basic proteins around which eukaryotic DNA is packaged. They are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine, which carry positive charges in their side chains. Eight histone molecules form a unit called the histone octamer. Leucine and phenylalanine are not basic amino acids. So option A.

The repressor made by the i gene normally binds the operator and stops RNA polymerase from transcribing z, y and a; lactose, the inducer, frees the operator by binding the repressor and inactivating it. Here the mutant repressor cannot bind the inducer, so it stays on the operator even when lactose is present. The genes z, y and a are then not transcribed, so they cannot be translated either. A, B and D all need the operator to be free, so option C.

After electrophoresis, the DNA fragments are stained with ethidium bromide (B) and, when exposed to UV light, are seen as bright orange bands (D). The separated bands are cut out of the agarose gel and extracted, a step called elution (A). A chromogenic substrate gives blue colonies, not blue DNA bands: it is used to screen recombinant bacteria by insertional inactivation of the \(\beta\)-galactosidase gene. So C is the statement that is not true.
why: never said why C is wrong

solution: Primary consumers feed directly on the producers (green plants), so they are herbivores. Carnivores and predators that eat herbivores are secondary or higher consumers. Parasites live on or in a host and draw nourishment from it; they are not the level of a food chain that feeds on plants. So option C.

(a) is true: energy flows in one direction, from the sun to producers and then to consumers, and does not cycle back. (b) is true: the pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted, because some energy is lost as heat at every trophic level. (c) is false: transfer of energy between trophic levels follows the 10 per cent law, under which only about 10 per cent of the energy at one level reaches the next. So (a) and (b) only, option B.

A is true: detritivores such as earthworms break detritus into smaller particles, which is fragmentation. B is true: humus is further degraded by some microbes, releasing inorganic nutrients, which is mineralisation. C is true: water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts, which is leaching. D is false: the detritus food chain begins with detritus, that is dead organic matter. E is false: earthworms breaking detritus into smaller particles is fragmentation, while catabolism is the breakdown of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacterial and fungal enzymes. So A, B and C only, option A.

B is incorrect: an algal bloom is the excessive growth of planktonic algae caused by large amounts of nutrients in water, and it causes deterioration of water quality and fish mortality rather than improving them. A is correct: the algae and their decomposition use up the dissolved oxygen, killing aquatic organisms. C is correct: water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and upsets the ecosystem dynamics. D is correct: some toxic substances in industrial waste water increase in concentration at successive trophic levels, which is biomagnification. So option B.
why: said water quantity; NCERT: water quality

solution: CNG burns more efficiently than petrol or diesel, leaving very little unburnt (A); it is cheaper than petrol or diesel (C); and it cannot be siphoned off by thieves or adulterated like petrol or diesel (D). B is false: a bus cannot run on CNG with its diesel engine unchanged, so the switch needed converted or new engines and was not a low-cost reuse of the same engine. So option B.
why: garbled (cheaper then petrol; burns more efficiently unlike)
